criteria.criterion: athena.toml defines the 'cannot affect' path patterns once, and every check that uses them refers to that single definition; no pattern list appears more than once.
criteria.evidence: From the diff: athena.toml has a single `[path_sets]` table with `prose = ["docs/**", "README.md", "CHANGELOG.md", "BRIEF.md"]`. The four fmt and clippy checks (change and study) say only `skip_when_only = ["prose"]`, and Config::skip_patterns resolves those names. No pattern list appears twice.

criteria.criterion: A change touching only studies/**, any .json file, Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock, or any .rs file never skips the test check (covered by a unit test of the skip decision).
criteria.evidence: The test check names no set, so CheckSpec::can_skip returns false for any path. The unit test the_skip_decision_is_safe_by_default (athena-cap-change) asserts this for run.rs, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, studies/x/result.json, data.json and more. It also asserts that fmt and clippy are not skipped for these paths.

criteria.criterion: Docs files that tests read (docs/non-rust-files.md, docs/architecture.md, docs/enforcement.md and any others found by grep for reads in tests) do not allow skipping the test check.
criteria.evidence: The test check has no skip_when_only, so no change can skip it. The unit test asserts this for docs/non-rust-files.md, docs/architecture.md, docs/enforcement.md, README.md and athena.toml. A comment in athena.toml explains why: the policy tests scan every tracked file.

criteria.criterion: Config parsing rejects or defaults safely: a check with no path set always runs; an empty change list runs every check.
criteria.evidence: skip_when_only uses serde(default) and is empty by default. can_skip returns false when there are no paths or no patterns. The unit test asserts `!can_skip(empty)` and that a check with no sets is not skipped. Validation rejects malformed patterns and unknown set names, and the tests bad_path_sets_are_rejected and path_patterns_have_three_forms cover this.

summary: The retry fixes the earlier attempt's three findings, and I found no blocker or major problem. Patterns that cannot affect a check are now written once, in a new `[path_sets]` table in athena.toml, which holds one set named `prose`. The fmt and clippy checks of both the change and study capabilities point to that set through `skip_when_only`. A check is skipped only when the change list has at least one path and every path matches a pattern in the check's sets. Any other path, an empty change list, or a check that names no set runs the check. The test check names no set, so it is never skipped. That covers code, Cargo files, JSON files, studies/ and the docs that tests read. Config parsing rejects bad patterns and unknown set names. I ran `cargo test -p athena-core`: both new run-loop tests passed. The docs-only test records fmt and clippy as passed with the note "not run: no changed path can affect it" and shows the test check ran. The studies/*.json test shows every check ran. I also ran fmt, clippy and `cargo test --locked`; all passed. D79 in docs/decisions.md, a CHANGELOG line and an M31 row in docs/enforcement.md document the change. No build.rs exists, and a search found no include_str! of docs/, README.md, CHANGELOG.md or BRIEF.md, so skipping clippy on prose-only changes looks safe. The listed deliverables crates/athena-data/src/config.rs… wait, rather: two listed deliverables were not touched, crates/athena-cli/tests/common/mod.rs and crates/athena-cap-change's siblings are fine; only crates/athena-cli/tests/common/mod.rs is unchanged, and nothing needed it.
